static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.educational_background: American literature and Bachelor's degree in education
static_traits.family_status: Living alone in a big city
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of friends, but has not yet shared the sense of failure with them; relationships with family and friends strained due to negative beliefs
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy or counseling before; no similar psychological problem history
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly logical; negative tone, tending toward all-or-nothing, overgeneralization, and mental filtering; cooperative and willing to try, but Self-denial marked

basic_info.main_problem: I feel graduating from university with a 3.5 GPA is a waste; I could have done better. This belief makes me feel pain and failure.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of failure are affecting my self-esteem and my overall view of life, so I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: University years spent under long-term pressure of academic performance and social expectations; immediately after graduation, viewed the 3.5 GPA as not up to standard, thus producing and maintaining the sense of failure.
For many years after graduation, repeatedly compares with classmates' higher GPAs, aggravating self-belittling and frustration experiences.

Not actively seeking help, hoping time will dilute the problem; not yet sharing the sense of failure with the supportive friend group, straining relationships; personal life Decreased motivation (such as less hiking).

core_beliefs: My worth depends on academic grades
If not the best, then it is failure
I am not good enough / I am a failure

special_situations.event: When alone recalling university experiences and her own 3.5 GPA
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the GPA is not a higher score, it means I wasted university; I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluating oneself with all-or-nothing standards, negating the positive gains of university years to maintain 'high standards'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My university years were wasted; I am a failure

special_situations.event: When comparing academic grades with classmates or seeing classmates' higher GPA
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot outperform classmates, I do not deserve recognition, which means I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently engages in social comparison, belittling herself to 'spur' herself on
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When family or friends discuss academic performance / achievement topics
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must achieve the results others expect in order to have value, otherwise will be looked down on
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids sharing true feelings to avoid being judged or disappointed
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am a failure

special_situations.event: When reviewing the university experience, facing positive experiences (such as being commended in teaching practice, making friends)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only GPA counts as real achievement; nothing else matters
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Filters information, focuses only on grade numbers, actively ignoring positive evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those good experiences do not count

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen (proving self-worth through notable achievements)
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated for not reaching high standards, losing value and being shamed in comparison
defense_goal: Maintaining 'security' with harsh self-standards, avoiding being negated by external evaluation
Reducing expressions of vulnerability and not sharing the sense of failure for Self-protection

object_relations.object_representation: Critical others who use grades as the only standard (society/classmates/family)

object_relations.self_representation: An individual whose efforts are obscured by numbers
object_relations.object_representation: A judge who only looks at scores and ignores diverse achievements

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to conduct reality testing, identify cognitive distortions, and consider positive experiences during university
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the counselor is downplaying one's standards and ignoring 'facts', experiencing one's harsh inner critic being challenged (transference: experiencing inner harshness as external denial)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain Empathy and affirmation, gentle tone, slow pace; first validate feelings, then invite concrete examples with open-ended questions; avoid arguing over numbers, help connect emotions with meaning.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing whether to share feelings of failure with friends or family, or exploring interpersonal impact
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes expressing vulnerability will trigger judgment and worsen relationships, so tends to stay silent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Acknowledging concerns in a supportive tone; using gentle rhetorical questions to distinguish 'worry' from 'evidence', encouraging small, controllable sharing attempts and boundary-setting.

manifestations: Defining the 3.5 GPA as 'university wasted', negating interpersonal and practical growth during university years
Measures self-worth by a single metric (GPA), ignoring the diverse meanings of life
outcomes: Life Decreased motivation (such as less hiking)
Overall outlook on life turning negative

manifestations: Having supportive friends yet not sharing the sense of failure
Interpersonal relationships strained due to negative beliefs
outcomes: Increased emotional burden, lacking the buffer of external support

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes 'only a higher GPA counts as success' as a rigid standard
Defines self-worth by a single score, ignoring diverse achievements

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Emphasizing one's own shortcomings and negating positive evidence in sessions

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not sharing the sense of failure with friends, turning energy toward self-rumination and self-criticism
Participates less in previous interests like hiking

exception_events.target_problem: When recalling university experiences or comparing with classmates, the client usually sinks into negative thinking of 'university wasted / I am a failure' and avoids expressing, leading to Low mood and Interpersonal tension.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Received commendation during university teaching internship, gaining concrete positive feedback and recognition; this experience reflects ability and growth, becoming exceptional evidence differing from the 'university wasted' narrative.
exception_events.reason: Different support: positive feedback and formal commendation from the internship mentor; different situation: practical teaching tasks with more diverse evaluation dimensions, showing ability beyond GPA.

positive_force: Has a supportive network of friends
Received commendation for university teaching practice, demonstrating teaching ability and practical experience
Current occupational performance stable, Work functioning not yet affected
Willing to seek counseling and try to change
negative_force: Frequently engages in social comparison, overly dependent on external evaluation
Cognitive biases like all-or-nothing, overgeneralization, mental filtering, and negating the positive
Takes GPA as the only standard of worth, ignoring other achievements
Not sharing vulnerability and the sense of failure, Interpersonal tension
Impaired self-esteem and life Decreased motivation

target_behavior.behavior: Recurring negative Automatic thoughts and self-labeling (such as 'university wasted' / 'I am a failure')
antecedent: Compares grades with classmates or sees others' higher GPAs
Family or friends talk about academic performance/achievements
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjection of high standards and dependence on external evaluation, forming the cognitive rule of defining self-worth by a single score
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a sense of control over standards through self-criticism, avoiding facing more complex self-evaluation and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-esteem, ongoing emotional distress, worsening overall outlook on life

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids sharing vulnerability and reduces interest participation (e.g. hiking)
antecedent: Plans social activities when feelings of failure arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries about being judged; shame and fear of relationship deterioration
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotions and possible negative evaluations to ease Anxiety short-term
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, Decreased support, quality of life and Decreased motivation
